label: FigS1.
title: Workflow variability sources and similarity metrics
legend: Supplemental Figure 1: scRNA-seq matrix generation and analysis overview. Red = sources of variability explored in this study; Blue = plots and metrics used to assess function similarity.

label: FigS2.
title: Seurat-like Scanpy arguments in a sequential pipeline
legend: Supplemental Figure 2: Seurat vs. Scanpy, aligned function arguments (Seurat-like arguments used in Scanpy), sequential analysis (data is run from start to end through each package without modification). (A) Filtering and HVG selection analysis UpSet plots consisting of sets of (i) cells, (ii) genes, and (iii) HVGs. (B) (i) PCA analysis through projection onto the first 2 PCs. (ii) Scree plot and the sine of eigenvectors. Black lines = point mapping between conditions. (C) KNN/SNN analysis through SNN neighborhood Jaccard index and degree ratio (Seurat/Scanpy) per cell. (D) Clustering and UMAP analysis through UMAP plots of Seurat (left) and Scanpy (right), with the alluvial diagram (middle) showing cluster assignment mapping and degree of cluster agreement. Numbers at the bottom of the alluvial diagram represent the total number of clusters in each group. (E) Differential expression analysis UpSet plot through overlap of all significant (p < 0.05) marker genes across all clusters.

label: FigS3.
title: Default Seurat vs Scanpy with controlled step inputs
legend: Supplemental Figure 3: Seurat vs. Scanpy, default function arguments, controlled analysis (the data created by Scanpy is replaced by the data created by Seurat following each step, such that each step sees identical input). (A) Filtering and HVG selection analysis UpSet plots consisting of sets of (i) cells, (ii) genes, and (iii) HVGs. (B) (i) PCA analysis through projection onto the first 2 PCs. (ii) Scree plot and the sine of eigenvectors. Black lines = point mapping between conditions. (C) KNN/SNN analysis through SNN neighborhood Jaccard index and degree ratio (Seurat/Scanpy) per cell. (D) Clustering and UMAP analysis through UMAP plots of Seurat (left) and Scanpy (right), with the alluvial diagram (middle) showing cluster assignment mapping and degree of cluster agreement. Numbers at the bottom of the alluvial diagram represent the total number of clusters in each group. (E) (i) Differential expression analysis through overlap of all significant (p < 0.05) marker genes across all clusters. (ii) Differential expression analysis with matched clusters of overlap of all markers. (iii) Differential expression analysis with matched clusters of logFC similarity. (iv) Differential expression analysis with matched clusters of adjusted p-value similarity. Dataset: 10k PBMC. Dataset: 10k PBMC.

label: FigS11.
title: Read-downsampling thresholds across pipeline metrics
legend: Supplemental Figure 11: Pipeline consistency metrics as a function of the fraction of reads retained after read downsampling. (A) Jaccard index for detected cells. (B) Jaccard index for detected genes. (C) Jaccard index for selected HVGs. (D) Mean of difference in PC loadings for PCs 1-3. (E) Median log(SNN degree ratio). (F) Adjusted Rand Index of cluster assignments. (G) Median Jaccard index of UMAP-derived KNN graphs for each cell. (H) Jaccard index of sets of significant (p < 0.05) marker genes across all clusters. (I) Jaccard index of all markers. (J) CCC of log fold changes. (K) Fraction of genes whose adjusted p-value crosses the 0.05 threshold after downsampling. Orange = Seurat workflow; Blue = Scanpy workflow; lighter lines = replicates of downsampling across random seeds; dashed line = metric recorded when comparing between Seurat and Scanpy when both pipelines are run on the full, non-downsampled dataset using their default parameters (Figure 1, S3).

label: FigS15.
title: Cluster 0-9 DE and Enrichr differences between Seurat and Scanpy
legend: Supplemental Figure 15: Additional analysis underscores observed differences between Seurat and Scanpy in biologically-motivated downstream analysis on clusters 0-9. Each row represents repeated analysis on a cluster derived from the conditions of Supplemental Figure 3 (i.e., Seurat vs. Scanpy with default methods and controlled input preceding each step). (A) Volcano plots for differentially-expressed genes identified by Seurat. (B) Volcano plot for differentially-expressed genes identified by Scanpy. Biological significance thresholds used (dashed lines): | log F C| = 1 (vertical) and p = 0.05 (horizontal). Red = significantly upregulated; Blue = significantly downregulated; grey = no significant difference. (C) UpSet plots of the set comparison for the biologically significant (i.e., red and blue) genes selected from the volcano plots generated by Seurat and Scanpy. (D) Gene ontology analysis scatterplot from the Enrichr "pathway" database given the biologically significant genes identified by Seurat and Scanpy. Dataset: 10k PBMC.

label: FigS17.
title: Random seed variability in graphs, clustering, and UMAP
legend: Supplemental Figure 17: Variability introduced by differences in random seeds for functions involving randomness. (A) Seurat SNN graph generation (Annoy), with different seeds for KNN graph generation. (B) Seurat clustering (Louvain), with different seeds for Louvain; and UMAP-projection (uwot), with different seeds for UMAP projection. (C) Seurat KNN graph generation from UMAP space, with different seeds for UMAP projection. (D) Seurat clustering (Leiden) and UMAP projection from UMAP space, with different seeds for UMAP projection. (E) Scanpy SNN graph generation (NNDescent), with different seeds for KNN graph generation. (F) Scanpy clustering (Leiden), with different seeds for Leiden; and UMAP-projection (UMAP-learn), with different seeds for UMAP projection. (G) Scanpy KNN graph generation from UMAP space, with different seeds for UMAP projection. (H) Scanpy clustering (Leiden) and UMAP projection from UMAP space, with different seeds for UMAP projection. Dataset: 10k PBMC.

label: FigS18.
title: KNN vs SNN graph construction and pruning behavior
legend: Supplemental Figure 18: Comparison of KNN and SNN graphs. (A) KNN graph (k=3) constructed with the approximate Annoy algorithm (directedness not shown). Black = incorrectly added edges; Green = incorrectly omitted edges. (B) SNN graph with Seurat's pruning method. An example hub node is marked with *. An example peripheral node is marked with **. Note: the SNN graph with Scanpy's method is simply the undirected KNN graph.

label: FigS19.
title: How Seurat and Scanpy generate and reuse KNN/SNN graphs
legend: Supplemental Figure 19: Schematic of protocol describing generation and downstream use of KNN and SNN graphs. Top is for Seurat, bottom is for Scanpy. KNN(i) refers to the full set of k-nearest neighbors for cell i. Bold = function/method name; Italics = outside package utilized.
